incidents.vector: Active exploitation of an authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-0257) in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS portal and gateway components to establish unauthorized VPN sessions.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed attackers probing and connecting to GlobalProtect gateways after the CVE was added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29; only a fraction of probed devices established sessions and no lateral movement has yet been confirmed.

incidents.victim: US gas stations / fuel storage operators
incidents.vector: Targeting of internet-exposed automatic tank gauge (ATG) systems, which carry known command-injection, authentication-bypass and hardcoded-credential vulnerabilities.
incidents.impact: A joint notice from CISA, FBI, NSA, DoE, EPA, TSA, DOT and USDA warned of malicious activity against ATGs that could let attackers alter tank readings, disable safety alerts or cut operators off from data; Shadowserver found ~909 exposed US devices, the vast majority of the global total.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Southeast Asia scam syndicates (China-linked organized crime)
incidents.vector: Industrial-scale cryptocurrency 'pig butchering' investment fraud run from compounds in Cambodia, Laos and Burma, abusing US social media, email and internet infrastructure.
incidents.impact: DOJ's Scam Center Strike Force 'Disruption Week' saw industry voluntarily interrupt 1.4M+ social media and email accounts and freeze $3.8M in crypto; IC3 reported crypto investment-fraud losses rose to over $7.2B in 2025.

incidents.vector: A compromised GitHub account was used to push a self-propagating credential-stealing worm variant ('Miasma', built from TeamPCP's leaked Mini Shai-Hulud code) into Red Hat's package channel.
incidents.impact: Red Hat pulled 32 tainted packages downloaded roughly 117,000 times per week after the malware harvested developer credentials and secrets; part of a cascading supply-chain campaign running since the September 2025 Shai-Hulud worm.

incidents.victim: Instagram account holders (incl. Obama White House, US Space Force)
incidents.vector: Social-engineering of Meta's AI support assistant: using a local-area VPN and the password-reset chat flow, attackers tricked the bot into linking an attacker-controlled email and issuing a one-time reset code.
incidents.impact: Pro-Iran hackers briefly defaced high-value Instagram accounts with pro-Iranian messaging and hijacked valuable short usernames; accounts with MFA enabled were unaffected, and Meta pushed an emergency patch.

incidents.vector: Smart-contract bugs, multisig-wallet manipulation and exploitation of legacy DeFi protocols and cross-chain bridges.
incidents.impact: A wave of late-May/early-June heists hit Verus ($11.6M, ~75% later returned), DxSale ($7.3M), Gravity Bridge ($5.4M), StablR ($2.8M) and RetoSwap ($2.7M in Monero).

incidents.vector: A publicly exposed cloud server left without a password.
incidents.impact: More than 3.4 million scanned images — including driver's licenses and legal and financial documents tied to inmates — were exposed for at least a week before being secured.

incidents.vector: Uncoordinated public release of working zero-day exploit code for Windows by a researcher known as 'Nightmare Eclipse', making PoCs immediately available to attackers.
incidents.impact: Three of the disclosed flaws (BlueHammer, UnDefend, RedSun) have been exploited in live intrusions and added to CISA's KEV catalog; three further unpatched zero-days were released, with more threatened for the July 14 Patch Tuesday.

incidents.vector: A poisoned Nx Console VS Code extension (v18.95.0, CVE-2026-48027) auto-distributed via the editor's update mechanism compromised a GitHub employee's device.
incidents.impact: Attackers exfiltrated internal GitHub repositories and demanded $50,000, threatening to leak the source code; part of a broader supply-chain wave that also compromised OpenAI employee devices via the TanStack library (CVE-2026-45321).

incidents.vector: The 'Megalodon' campaign injected malicious GitHub Action workflows into public repositories to harvest CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials and tokens.
incidents.impact: CISA warned the campaign abused automated-account commits (especially after May 18, 2026) to steal pipeline secrets across development and deployment environments, urging mass credential rotation.

incidents.vector: Phishing compromise of a single employee account granting access to a limited portion of Carnival's IT environment.
incidents.impact: Attackers copied personal data — names, addresses, dates of birth, driver's license and passport numbers — on nearly 6 million people; the group claimed to release 8.7M records after a failed extortion attempt.

incidents.vector: Use of compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access land and real-estate data.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole roughly 600,000 records containing real names, cadastral information and other real-estate details from Lithuania's state registry.

incidents.vector: Data theft surfaced via the ShinyHunters dark-web leak portal, where Charter's name was listed.
incidents.impact: The US telecom confirmed a security breach after appearing on the extortion group's leak site; the scope of stolen data has not yet been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion with data theft for extortion.
incidents.impact: The Play ransomware group is extorting MyPillow, claiming to have stolen sensitive financial documents from its corporate network; the company has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.victim: Australian MP Zali Steggall and staff
incidents.vector: Compromise of the WhatsApp account of an independent MP and three staffers, believed to be part of a campaign targeting messaging accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: A suspected foreign state actor breached the accounts in March; attribution is unconfirmed but consistent with a Russian campaign against Signal and WhatsApp accounts of politicians.

incidents.victim: Oregon state government office (and other US victims)
incidents.vector: Romanian national obtained unauthorized access to a computer on an Oregon state government network in 2021 and sold dark-web access, with PII samples, to prospective buyers.
incidents.impact: Catalin Dragomir was sentenced to 56 months in federal prison for selling network access to numerous US and global victims, causing losses of at least $250,000.

incidents.vector: Intrusions into two unnamed government agencies that initially went undetected.
incidents.impact: The compromised networks store the data of millions of citizens; the Vietnamese government has opened an investigation into the breaches.

incidents.vector: Breach and leak of sensitive internal documents from the Russian state-linked disinformation group.
incidents.impact: Leaked files detailed active influence operations across Armenia, France, Ukraine, Germany, Moldova and Norway and named local collaborators including a retired US general and a former Bundestag member.

incidents.victim: UN World Food Programme (Gaza aid recipients)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to data stored in WFP's self-registration application (SRA) used exclusively in Palestine.
incidents.impact: Names, identification numbers, phone numbers and neighborhood-level location data of roughly 600,000 Palestinian households in Gaza were exposed; WFP suspended the platform while investigating.
